claim: Diabetes mellitus (DM) increases risk for pulmonary tuberculosis (TB).
source: Diabetes mellitus (DM) increases risk for pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) and adverse treatment outcomes.
evidence: Supported by citation to Critchley et al., 2017 in the Introduction section

claim: Diabetes mellitus increases risk for adverse TB treatment outcomes.
source: Diabetes mellitus (DM) increases risk for pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) and adverse treatment outcomes.
evidence: Supported by citation to Critchley et al., 2017 in the Introduction section

claim: Systemic hyper-inflammation is characteristic in people with TB and concurrent DM (TBDM) at baseline.
source: Systemic hyper-inflammation is characteristic in people with TB and concurrent DM (TBDM) at baseline, but the impact of TB treatment on this pattern has not been determined.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as established finding, supported by citations in the manuscript

claim: Principal component analysis revealed virtually complete separation of TBDM from TB individuals in both Indian and Brazilian cohorts at baseline.
source: Principal component analysis revealed virtually complete separation of TBDM from TB individuals in both cohorts at baseline, with hyper-inflammation in TBDM that continued through treatment completion at six months.

claim: Hyper-inflammation in TBDM continued through treatment completion at six months.
source: Principal component analysis revealed virtually complete separation of TBDM from TB individuals in both cohorts at baseline, with hyper-inflammation in TBDM that continued through treatment completion at six months.

claim: By one year after treatment completion, there was substantial convergence of mediator levels between TBDM and TB groups within the India cohort.
source: By one year after treatment completion, there was substantial convergence of mediator levels between groups within the India cohort.
evidence: Based on plasma cytokine measurements at month 18 in the India cohort

claim: Non-resolving systemic inflammation in TBDM comorbidity could reflect delayed lesion sterilization.
source: Non-resolving systemic inflammation in TBDM comorbidity could reflect delayed lesion sterilization or non-resolving sterile inflammation.

claim: Persistent inflammation in TBDM portends unfavorable long-term outcomes including risk for recurrent TB.

claim: DM is associated with increased risk to become infected with Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
source: It is now well established that diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with increased the risk to become infected with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), to progress from latent infection to active pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) disease, and to suffer adverse TB outcomes including delayed sputum conversion on treatment, treatment failure, death, and recurrent TB (Critchley et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Critchley et al., 2017

claim: DM is associated with increased risk to progress from latent infection to active pulmonary tuberculosis disease.

evidence: Supported by citation to Critchley et al., 2017

claim: Restrepo et al. were the first to describe increased expression of a broad range of cytokines from antigen-stimulated whole blood from patients with concurrent TB and DM as compared to TB alone.

claim: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of TBDM comorbidity is driven by a higher lung bacterial burden and/or by impaired counter regulatory mechanisms.
source: We hypothesized that the hyperinflammatory phenotype of TBDM comorbidity is driven by a higher lung bacterial burden and/or by impaired counter regulatory mechanisms that normally limit bystander tissue injury from protective immune responses.

claim: There was no difference in the proportion of TB or TBDM participants who reported current or past alcohol consumption in the India cohort.

claim: The median HbA1c in TBDM participants was 10.0%, indicating poor glycemic control.

claim: Median BMI was higher in the KDM group compared to the NDM group.
